subject: vector slicing in multivariate time series models

messages.author: 9dd9ea947d797759
messages.subject: vector slicing in multivariate time series models
parts:
The AR(1) example on pages 59-60 of the STAN manual says that

tail(y, N - 1) ~ normal(alpha + beta * head(y, N - 1), sigma);

is more efficient than

for (n in 2:N)
y[n] ~ normal(alpha + beta * y[n-1], sigma);

Is there an analogous way to do this in a multivariate AR(1)? For example, with

matrix[2, 2] beta;
vector[2] y[N];

I'd like to do a vectorized calculation involving this:

beta * head(y, N-1)

instead of a loop involving this:

for (n in 2:N){
      beta * y[n-1]
}

The former gives me:

SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="multiply"
    arg 0 type=matrix
    arg 1 type=vector[1]

Example attached. Thanks.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] vector slicing in multivariate time series models
parts:
> On Nov 30, 2014, at 2:51 PM, Matthew Spencer <matt.sp...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ... with

>
> matrix[2, 2] beta;
> vector[2] y[N];
>
> I'd like to do a vectorized calculation involving this:
>
> beta * head(y, N-1)
>

What do you expect that to give you? head(y, N-1) is
an array of vectors, and we don't support multiplication
for arrays of vectors. The error you got

> SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:
> no matches for function name="multiply"
> arg 0 type=matrix
> arg 1 type=vector[1]

is saying that the second argument to the multiplication,
that is head(y, N-1) is an array of vectors. Stan doesn't
support multiplying a matrix by an array of vectors.

Would you expect to get an array of vectors out? The only
way to do that is to allocate the array of vectors and
assign the members.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] vector slicing in multivariate time series models
parts:
On Sunday, November 30, 2014 3:22:36 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Would you expect to get an array of vectors out?  The only
way to do that is to allocate the array of vectors and
assign the members.

I think the same thing could be accomplished if y were declared as a two-column matrix and then using the block() function to select all but the last row.

Ben

That sounds like a good suggestion, but I couldn't get it to work, because multi_normal_log doesn't allow argument 0 to be a matrix:

block(y, 1, 2, 2, N) ~ multi_normal(alpha + to_vector(beta * block(y, 1, 1, 2, N-1)), sigma);

arg 2 type=matrix

(and I'm guessing that to_vector isn't doing the right thing either: is it equivalent to the vec operator?). It seems like you'd need a lot of conversions between data types to get this to work.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] vector slicing in multivariate time series models
parts:
Even a (1 x N) or (M x 1) matrix is still a matrix type if
that's the return type (as it is for block()).

You can flatten an (M x 1) matrix to a vector with to_vector()
and similarly for a (1 x N) matrix and to_row_vector(). [You can
cross them up if you want to build in a transpose.]

- Bob
